provenance_note: The Palmer adult census and durable-extinction labels are already known. A prior validation branch fetched the chick-production dataset but did not produce a successful result for this size-productivity or pre-extinction-performance endpoint. This contract freezes the new endpoint, estimability gates, null and decision rules before executing them.

source.title: Adelie penguin colony-specific chick production, 1991, present.

biological_question: Before invoking social facilitation or predation, is reproductive output itself density dependent within Palmer Adelie breeding colonies?

hypotheses.H1_size_productivity: Within the same island and breeding season, larger colony codes have higher chicks per breeding pair than smaller colony codes.
hypotheses.H2_within_colony: The size-productivity relationship remains positive after controlling stable colony identity and shared island-season conditions.
hypotheses.H3_pre_extinction: Colony codes that will undergo durable extinction have lower reproductive output in the immediately preceding breeding season than contemporaneous survivors.

season_definition: For January chick censuses, season_start_year = calendar year(time) - 1, matching the preceding November breeding season.

row_eligibility.biological_cap: require num_chicks <= 2 * num_breeding_pairs; fail closed if violated
row_eligibility.duplicate_rule: fail closed if more than one usable row exists for island, colony_code and season_start_year

primary_H1.group_eligibility: at least 3 usable colony codes, positive total chicks, and non-zero SD of log1p breeding-pair count
primary_H1.group_statistic: OLS slope of chicks_per_pair on standardized log1p pair count with an intercept; because predictor is centered, slope equals sum(z*y)/sum(z^2)
primary_H1.paper_statistic: equal-weight mean group slope across all eligible island-seasons
primary_H1.estimability_gate: at least 15 eligible island-seasons and at least 60 usable colony-season rows

primary_null.name: equal-per-pair chick-slot productivity
primary_null.conditioning: Within each eligible island-season, condition on observed breeding-pair counts and observed total chick count.
primary_null.capacity: Each breeding pair contributes two potential chick slots, so colony capacity is 2 * num_breeding_pairs.
primary_null.simulation: Allocate the observed total chicks across colony capacities using a multivariate hypergeometric draw. This preserves the biological 0-2 chicks-per-pair cap and makes expected chick production proportional to breeding-pair abundance.
primary_null.p_value: one-sided upper-tail Monte Carlo p with +1 correction

secondary_H2_two_way_fixed_effect.eligibility: colonies with at least 5 usable seasons; island-seasons must contain at least 2 retained colonies
secondary_H2_two_way_fixed_effect.model: OLS of chicks_per_pair on log1p pair count with colony fixed effects and island-season fixed effects
secondary_H2_two_way_fixed_effect.null: Use the same multivariate-hypergeometric chick allocations and refit the identical fixed-effect model for each joint simulation.
secondary_H2_two_way_fixed_effect.role: tests whether the association is not solely due to stable colony quality or shared annual conditions

secondary_H3_pre_extinction.event_labels: Use durable-extinction transitions from PALMER_COLONY_EXTINCTION_HAZARD_V1 with its primary three-zero rule and right-censoring.
secondary_H3_pre_extinction.join: For transition start_year t, join chick-production season_start_year t by island and colony_code.
secondary_H3_pre_extinction.risk_set_eligibility: at least one future durable-extinction colony and one non-event survivor with usable chick data in the same island-start_year risk set.
secondary_H3_pre_extinction.group_statistic: mean chicks_per_pair among future-extinction colonies minus mean among non-event colonies
secondary_H3_pre_extinction.paper_statistic: equal-weight mean group contrast across informative risk sets
secondary_H3_pre_extinction.estimability_gate: at least 5 informative risk sets and at least 8 future-extinction colonies with chick data
secondary_H3_pre_extinction.null: Within each informative risk set, condition on joined colony pair counts and total chicks and allocate chicks by the same multivariate-hypergeometric equal-per-pair null; keep extinction labels fixed.
secondary_H3_pre_extinction.p_value: one-sided lower-tail Monte Carlo p with +1 correction

decision_rule.H1_support: primary mean slope > 0 and upper-tail p <= 0.05
decision_rule.strong_density_dependence: H1 supported and H2 coefficient > 0 with upper-tail p <= 0.05
decision_rule.mechanistic_interpretation: Only strong_density_dependence permits saying the data contain an Allee-like reproductive-performance signature. Even then, do not identify social facilitation or skua predation uniquely. H3 adds temporal coherence if supported.

interpretation_boundaries: A positive size-productivity relationship is consistent with density-dependent reproductive performance but can also arise from transient habitat or predator conditions correlated with colony size.
Colony fixed effects reduce confounding by stable patch quality but do not prove causality.
Do not interpret failure of H1 as evidence that colony size has no ecological relevance; it only rejects this reproductive-output pathway.
Do not use raw chicks-per-pair asymptotic standard errors as the primary inference; the hypergeometric null is the inferential gate.
Do not change the chick-slot capacity, eligibility thresholds, tail direction or event definition after the outcomes are opened.
